Q: Ctrl+Shift+E inserts special characters into file instead of showing Explorer Pane in VS Code A:

This is a very good workaround.

Open terminal, run ibus-setup (or sudo ibus-setup if needed). A GUI dialog will open.

Go to the 'Emoji' tab --> Emoji annotation ellipsis(...) buttton --> Delete 'Ctrl + Shift + E' entry --> OK.

That's it. Works for me on Ubuntu 20.04. You can still access emojis using Ctrl + .(period).

Q: Error: NOT SUPPORTED: keyword "id", use "$id" for schema ID following Angular13 upgrade A:

I fixed it myself :)

I cloned the package https://github.com/migalons/angular-wdio-builder and upgraded the following packages:

"@angular-devkit/architect": "^0.1300.1",
"@angular-devkit/core": "^13.0.1"

I published the package and updated my Angluar.json to use it and I don't get the error!

Q: Getting this error out of a sudden java.lang.IllegalStateException: Request cannot be executed; I/O reactor status: STOPPED A:

Change the condition of getHighLevelClient() to if (highLevelClient != null && highLevelClient.getLowLevelClient().isRunning())

which means if the low level client (RestClient) is not running, you should renew the client, that works for me.

Q: ReactJS: Render Math Equation's svg in pdf A:

I'm using InDesign to make the PDF, and it works. In my setup, I use math-svg-mcp to generate the SVGs. That server also returns some metadata required to perfectly base-align inline expressions. This post explains it.

Q: Feeling stuck after 2–3 years of C++ — normal learning curve or wrong approach? A:

I think problem is C++ is can adapt to many programming styles. in C++ you can.

  • Procedural (like C)
  • OOP
  • Polymorphism by OOP, Function/Operator overloading, templates
  • meta programming (templates)
  • low-level (access hardware, create own crazy container)
  • high-level (STD lib, abstraction like std::ostream)

so you don't need to know everything. Just know what C++ can do and what is your style is enough.

But fundamental of computer science (data structure, stack/heap, process, pointer, ...) is still important.
